01 / Coverage you can audit

The original README claimed coverage through 2019, but its supplied CSV actually ended in 2016. This edition uses one consistent, attributed source for both match and ball-by-ball data, with raw files and checksums retained. No-result matches remain in the descriptive analysis and are excluded from winner-model training.

These are records available from Cricsheet, not a claim that every scheduled fixture has ball-by-ball coverage. The last available match date in this snapshot is 2026-05-31.

02 / Teams, toss and chasing

The toss winner also won 51.38% of 1,234 decided matches. Chasing teams won 54.39% of 1,195 eligible regulation matches, excluding recorded rain-method results and tied/Super Over matches.

These are historical associations. Venue, opposition, conditions and era all influence the decision to chase, so the difference is not a causal effect of choosing to field.

05 / Honest prediction evaluation

The selected random forest achieved 45.2% accuracy on 73 decided matches in 2026. The training-prior baseline achieved 42.5%. Model log loss was 0.687, versus 0.695 for the baseline (lower is better). This is a measured experimental result, not a guaranteed advantage.

Model Accuracy (%) Log loss Brier score ROC AUC
Random forest 45.21 0.69 0.25 0.48
Training-prior baseline 42.47 0.69 0.25 0.50

Accuracy 95% Wilson interval: 34.3%–56.6%. The interval is approximate and does not account for dependence between matches.

Training: 2008–2024 · Selection: 2025 · Held-out test: 2026. Candidate selection uses validation log loss. Model weights stay fixed throughout the test season; history features update only after earlier dates.

Inputs are the two teams, venue, toss outcome, batting order, earlier Elo ratings, last-ten-match win form, smoothed head-to-head history, scoring rates and experience. Current-match scores, player-of-match awards and winning margins never enter the predictor. Team-order mirroring ensures that swapping the teams reverses their probabilities.

Validation comparison

model matches accuracy log_loss brier_score roc_auc accuracy_ci95_low accuracy_ci95_high
Logistic regression 71 0.54 0.70 0.26 0.52 0.42 0.65
Random forest 71 0.51 0.70 0.25 0.53 0.39 0.62

Both an evaluated holdout model and a separate model refitted on all decided matches are included. Line-ups, injuries, player availability, pitch and weather forecasts are outside this model. Results should be treated as an educational benchmark.

06 / Methods, sources and limitations

  • Source: Cricsheet IPL men's JSON download, maintained by Stephen Rushe. Format documentation.
  • Data license: Open Data Commons Attribution License 1.0. Original archive and license notices are preserved; derived tables contain normalized names and calculated statistics.
  • Only actual renames are consolidated. Deccan Chargers, Sunrisers Hyderabad, Pune Warriors and Rising Pune Supergiant remain distinct. Raw team and venue labels remain available.
  • Missing cities remain “Unknown”; no cities are invented. 51 source match records lack a city. 0 matches carry source missing-information flags.
  • Delivery counts include wides and no-balls. Bowling economy uses legal balls; byes, leg-byes and penalty extras are excluded from bowler-conceded runs. Batting balls exclude wides. Innings-level penalties are retained separately.
  • Phase bands use fixed over numbers. Player averages are blank when there are no dismissals or wickets. Counts can differ from official career totals where source coverage differs.
  • Checks cover unique keys, participating winners, run/extras arithmetic and innings reconciliation. They establish internal consistency, not independent scorecard verification of every ball.
